title: The open-closed sequence of strict semilinear module complexes
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion, and $a:U\hookrightarrow T$ its complementary quasi-compact open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and a strict inverse sequence $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ of sheaves of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Let $\mathscr S_T(B)$ be the category of strict semilinear systems: objects are $B_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_m$-linear maps $M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_m\to B_n}M_n$ for $m\geq n$, satisfying the identity and composition laws, and morphisms are componentwise module maps commuting with these transitions [def-coef-semilinear-system-models, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use the inverse ring systems $a^{-1}B$ and $i^{-1}B$ on $U$ and $Z$ and the ordinary module inverse/direct images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; at each level $a_!$ is module extension by zero along the localization $U_{\mathrm{proet}}=T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] for the ring sheaf $B_n$.

The componentwise functors $a^{-1},a_!,i^{-1},i_*$ define exact functors between these strict system categories, using the canonical scalar-restriction identifications for their transition maps. The open counit $\epsilon_a:a_!a^{-1}\to1$ and closed unit $\eta_i:1\to i_*i^{-1}$ are natural transformations of strict systems. For every cochain complex $C^\cdot$ of objects of $\mathscr S_T(B)$, not necessarily bounded, they give a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of strict systems
$$0\longrightarrow a_!a^{-1}C^\cdot\xrightarrow{\epsilon_a}C^\cdot\xrightarrow{\eta_i}i_*i^{-1}C^\cdot\longrightarrow0.$$
Its evaluations at every $n$ are the canonical ringed pro-etale counit-unit short exact sequences of $B_n$-module complexes. All its arrows commute with differentials and with the semilinear transitions, including composition of those transitions. These identifications commute with restriction of scalars along any compatible homomorphism of inverse ring systems $B_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ on $T$: the scalar comparisons for the open and closed terms carry the actual counit and unit to the corresponding ones, without changing their underlying additive sheaf maps. No coefficient-map flatness, constructibility, or normalization is required.

proof.text: Apply sequenceOpenCoefficients once to obtain normalized open coefficient comparisons. Apply sequenceOpenOrdinary to B with these comparisons to obtain an ordinary open datum and its actual Transitions equation. Apply the closed-system presentation theorem to obtain K with normalized exact closed operations.

For each ordinary system M apply the ordinary localization theorem to its actual open counit and closed unit. In each integer degree q apply it to C^q. The mapped adjunctions have exactly these degree components. Extensionality makes the composite chain map zero. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.shortExact_of_degreewise_shortExact gives monicity, epicity and exactness of the short complex. Convert ShortComplex exactness to ComposableArrows exactness and fill SequenceData with K and the given open datum. This step is written in Lean in sequenceData_of_closed and uses no boundedness hypothesis.

Given a compatible coefficient map B→D, repeat the preceding construction for D. Apply the coefficient-compatibility theorem to the two supplied localization data to obtain the four normalized comparisons and their actual counit/unit equations. Package the existential result.
